title: Perfect maps into principal support are power torsion
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], let f be a global function on X, and let T=V(f). If alpha:E \to E' is a morphism in D_QCoh(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category], E is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], and every cohomology sheaf of E' vanishes on X\setminus T, then f^n alpha=0 for some integer n\ge 0.

proof.text: Affine case, X=Spec(A), f in A. By the affine equivalence D(A)=D_QCoh(X) [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] and [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective], E is represented by a bounded complex P^bullet of finite projective A-modules and E' by a complex M^bullet of A-modules. Induct on the number of nonzero terms of P^bullet, for all alpha and all E' at once (a shift E'[k] of E' is again in D_QCoh and supported on T). If t is the largest index with P^t nonzero, the stupid-truncation triangle P^t[-t] \to P^bullet \to sigma_{<=t-1}P^bullet \to P^t[-t+1] gives an exact sequence Hom(sigma_{<=t-1}P^bullet,E') \to Hom(P^bullet,E') \to Hom(P^t[-t],E') of A-modules (Hom(-,E') is cohomological, and the maps are A-linear). If f^a kills the image of alpha in the right-hand group, then f^a alpha comes from some beta in the left-hand group, and f^b beta=0 by induction, so f^{a+b} alpha=0. This reduces to P^bullet a single finite projective module P in degree 0 (after shifting E'). Then Hom_{D(A)}(P,M^bullet)=H^0(Hom_A(P,M^bullet))=Hom_A(P,H^0(M^bullet)) because Hom_A(P,-) is exact. The cohomology sheaf H^0(E') is the sheaf associated with H^0(M^bullet) and vanishes on D(f) by hypothesis, so H^0(M^bullet)_f=0, i.e. every element of H^0(M^bullet) is killed by a power of f. The images of finitely many generators of P are killed by one power f^n, hence f^n alpha=0.

proof.text: Globalization. For a quasi-compact open W of X let P(W) be the statement of the lemma on W (all morphisms alpha:E\to E' in D_QCoh(O_W) with E perfect and E' supported on T intersect W, with f|_W). P holds for affine W by the previous step. Let W=U union V with U quasi-compact open, V affine open, and P true on U, V and U intersect V (the overlap is quasi-compact because X is quasi-separated). Given alpha on W, restrictions of perfect objects are perfect and of objects supported on T are supported on T, so there is an a with f^a alpha|_U=0 and f^a alpha|_V=0. The Mayer–Vietoris long exact sequence for Hom [lem-sc-derived-hom-mayer-vietoris] gives exactness of Hom(E|_{U\cap V},E'|_{U\cap V}[-1]) \to Hom(E,E') \to Hom(E|_U,E'|_U)\oplus Hom(E|_V,E'|_V), with Gamma(W,O_W)-linear maps; hence f^a alpha is the image of some beta:E|_{U\cap V}\to E'[-1]|_{U\cap V}. Since E'[-1] is supported on T, P(U intersect V) gives f^b beta=0, so f^{a+b} alpha=0. Thus P holds on U union V, and the induction principle on the quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme X [lem-sc-invert-s-cohomology-induction] gives P(X).
